text: An invoice is ready. Evidence is scattered, approvals stall, and nobody knows when money moved.
TallyGuard turns that handoff into five visible steps: read evidence, match records, apply finance policy, settle on Arc, and create an audit receipt. AI speeds the checks; finance keeps authority.
A requester starts with an invoice, purchase order, and delivery proof. Key fields are extracted, then confirmed by a person before the evidence is sealed.
Submission immediately shows one request ID, what passed, where the request is waiting, and what happens next. No funds are sent just because a request was submitted.
Finance sees the same ID and amount. It checks duplicate evidence, supplier, wallet, timing, and policy. This larger request needs independent approval.
A separate approver reviews the sealed evidence and records a reasoned decision. The agent can recommend, but it cannot authorize its own exception.
Approval is still not payment. Finance takes a separate settlement action. This public demo workspace simulates that transfer, so the filmed payment is not a live transaction.
The requester now sees the demo status, finance's note, settlement progress, and the final receipt under the same ID.
For low-value payments, finance may explicitly enable a no-touch policy: fifty USDC per request, five hundred per day, and an emergency stop. It is off unless finance turns it on.
A forty-USDC request enters. The invoice, order, delivery, supplier, wallet, and available budget must all satisfy the configured boundary.
Every required control passes, so this in-limit demo request settles automatically and the requester sees a receipt. There is no default AI authority over the treasury.

One planned run can reach four different outcomes: settle, route to a human, wait for the scheduled date, or hold for remediation. Every action stays inside the finance policy, with the reason recorded.
Compared with fragmented bank handoffs, Circle-controlled wallets and Arc USDC provide an always-on programmable settlement rail. Fiat entry and exit still involve banking partners.
50 test workflows. 40 confirmed Arc Testnet transfers. Independent historical proof.
TallyGuard: agent speed, finance control, proof on Arc.
